newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 15.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average closed above the 6,000 mark for the first time in its history, up 40.62 to 6,010, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.
- California's electric company Enova has agreed to merge with natural gas company Pacific Enterprises in a stock swap worth $2.8 billion.
- Intel Corp reported a 41-percent increase in quarterly profit due to a rise in personal computer sales.
- Chrysler Corp's quarterly profit nearly doubled from the same period a year ago. The company said it planned a nine-percent boost in its ability to make light trucks in 1997.
- The Canadian Auto Workers union's strike against General Motors Corp has forced a Cadillac assembly plant in Detroit to partly shut down.
- Archer Daniels Midland Co's agreement to plead guilty might signal that the Andreas family's reign over the big grain processer is coming to an end.
- A Metropolitan Life Insurance affiliate has agreed to buy real-estate advisory firm Aldrich, Eastman & Waltch for more than $70 million.
- Rite Aid Corp doesn't expect a federal commission to oppose its acquisition of Thrifty Payless Holdings.
- Pfizer Inc reported a 21-percent increase in quarterly earnings as a result of new drug sales.
- Mexico's peso ended at its lowest level of the year against the U.S. dollar.
- Philips Electronics NV said its second-half operating profits will probably not rise as much as had been anticipated.
- U.S. steel makers are losing their advantage against foreign competitors.
